ModelCharacter: A completely new 2005–09 Mainship 34 Trawler, unrelated in hull and dimensions to the classic MK I/II/III family. It is a much wider 14'3" semi-displacement flybridge cruiser with a full keel, wide sheltered walkways, spacious galley-down salon and either single- or twin-diesel propulsion.
DesignLineage: Introduced for 2005 as a new Mainship 34 Trawler rather than a continuation of the 1978–88 classic 34 hull.
At 14'3" beam and nearly 39 feet overall with pulpit, it is substantially larger than the 11'11"-beam classic MK I/II/III boats.
A single Yanmar diesel was standard and twin Yanmars were optional, giving displacement-speed economy or higher semi-planing performance depending configuration.
This 2005–09 model belongs to Mainship's later 350/390/400-era trawler design philosophy, not the classic 34 Mark lineage.
OwnershipCharacter: A far larger and more systems-heavy boat than the classic 34 despite sharing the model number. Single-engine boats preserve Mainship's economical-cruiser appeal, while twins add speed and redundancy; 14'3" beam, 15-foot clearance, generator/HVAC options and larger domestic systems materially increase storage and ownership cost.
